Description - Auth

Authenticates with the account name and the MD5 of the password and returns the session token used by every other call.

When the client sends it: start-up auto-login, after system resume (resume-login-delay), and as the re-login triggered by BadToken.

Outcomes (live): Ok with hamsterId/name/token; unknown user gives Forbidden; wrong password gives PermissionError (both with every other member nil); an empty body triggers an unhandled server exception (a:InternalServiceFault, HTTP 500). Neither ver nor client is enforced. A new Auth does not invalidate earlier tokens.

Client behaviour: Forbidden/PermissionError open the credentials dialog; other errors schedule a delayed re-login (delayed-login-interval, Inferred 20 s). A reply arriving while already logged in is discarded.

Routing. The path item declares the server http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=, so this operation resolves to http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc?op=/Auth. WCF ignores the query string and dispatches only on the SOAPAction header (verified live). The real client posts to the bare http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc; both URLs reach the same operation. A path suffix (.svc/Auth) does not work (a:DestinationUnreachable, see soapRestStylePath).

Wire format. POST with Content-Type: text/xml;charset=utf-8 (exact client bytes, no space; the server answers text/xml; charset=utf-8) and SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/Auth (unquoted). Body: SOAP 1.1 envelope, UTF-8, no indentation, parameters in the documented order (WCF silently drops out-of-order parameters). The client gzips the body (Content-Encoding: gzip).

Path notes

SOAP operation Auth. The path-level server makes the URL routable: WCF dispatches on SOAPAction and ignores the ?op=/Auth query.

Schema

Schema AuthRequestEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required AuthRequestEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 request envelope for Auth: <s:Envelope><s:Body><Auth xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/">…. No SOAP header is ever sent; xmlns:i is declared on the operation element only when a nil value is present.

    • @s:encodingStyle string optional = "http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/encoding/" namespace http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

      SOAP 1.1 encodingStyle attribute. The real client always writes it; the service accepts the envelope with or without it.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one operation element; no other content (this also makes the per-operation envelopes mutually exclusive).

      • <Auth> object required AuthRequest xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/

        Operation element Auth in http://chomikuj.pl/ (trailing slash is mandatory: with http://chomikuj.pl the parameters are not matched, see Service/wrong-operation-namespace).

        • <name> string required

          Account (hamster) login name, from the login dialog or [userinfo] login.

        • <passHash> string required

          Lower-case hex MD5 of the UTF-8 password, unsalted (stored as password-hash when "remember me" is set). Secret: never log.

        • <ver> integer (int32) required

          Protocol version; the client always sends 4 (PUSH 0x4 at). Not validated by the server (Auth/protocol-version-1).

        • <client> object optional ClientInfo

          Client identification; optional for the server.

          • <name> string required

            Client product name; the client always sends chomikbox.

          • <version> string required

            Client version; the client always sends 2.0.8.2.

Responses - 200, 500

200

SOAP response envelope. HTTP 200 is used for every service-level outcome, including errors: check AuthResult/status. Compressed (Content-Encoding: gzip) when the request accepts gzip.

Schema text/xml

Schema AuthResponseEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required AuthResponseEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 response envelope for Auth: <s:Envelope><s:Body><AuthResponse xmlns="http://chomikuj.pl/"><AuthResult …>.

    • <s:Body> object required

      Exactly one response element; no other content.

      • <AuthResponse> object required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl/
        • <AuthResult> object required AuthResult

          Result element; declares xmlns:i (XML Schema instance, for i:nil) and xmlns:a.

          • <a:status> string required Status xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Outcome of the call. The client accepts only Ok; BadToken triggers a re-login, anything else is an error.

            7 values
            • "Ok" Success. The only value the client treats as success.
            • "BadToken" Unknown, logged-out or otherwise invalid token. The client re-authenticates (Auth) once per message (message-relog-count=1) and resends the message with the new token; session-bound messages are dropped.
            • "Forbidden" Auth: user name does not exist. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "PermissionError" Auth: wrong password for an existing user. The client shows the credentials dialog.
            • "Error" Generic failure. Usually carries a reason in errorMessage (e.g. EmptyName, NameExistsAtDestination); FolderFiles with an unknown disposition returns Error with errorMessage nil (FolderFiles/invalid-disposition).
            • "NotEmptyOrNotExistsFolder" RemoveFolder with force=false on a folder that contains files, or on an unknown/removed folder id.
            • "WrongDisposition" FolderFiles: the disposition is a known value but not allowed for this call (download).
          • <a:errorMessage> string required nullable (i:nil) ErrorMessage xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Error detail for status=Error; nil otherwise.

          • <a:hamsterId> integer (int32) required xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Account id; 0 when the login failed.

          • <a:publisherId> string optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Always nil; not read by the client.

          • <a:name> string optional nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            Account name as stored by the service; nil when the login failed.

          • <a:token> string required nullable (i:nil) xmlns http://chomikuj.pl

            New session token; nil when the login failed. See Token.

Client vs live - discrepancies

Where the client's expected behaviour and the live service disagree, the spec follows the live behaviour (x-discrepancies):

  • The client always sends ver=4, but the server accepts any value.
  • client is optional for the server although the client always sends it.

Security notes - findings that concern Auth

  • C-01 High All client traffic uses plain HTTP (SOAP, upload, resume check, downloads, web login hand-off, updater, crash reports). The SOAP service also answers on HTTPS, but the client never uses it.
  • C-02 High The login credential passHash is an unsalted MD5 of the password, sent in clear in every Auth: it is password-equivalent and cheap to crack.
  • C-06 Medium The session token travels in clear in every SOAP body and as a URL query parameter (LoginFromBox?t=), where it becomes a full web session (ChomikSession) and can leak via logs, history and proxies.
  • S-01 Medium Account enumeration via Auth: an unknown user gets Forbidden, a known user with a wrong password gets PermissionError.
  • S-10 Info Concurrent sessions are allowed; Logout invalidates only its own token; no expiry was observed within about 45 minutes.
  • S-11 Info The client identity is not enforced: Auth accepts any ver and works without the client element, so any program can present itself as ChomikBox.

From x-security-notes in the spec. Ratings and scope are explained on Security & privacy.
